answer: Reverse-escrow handoff receipts. Each identity must hold a cedar-signed receipt co-signed by its prior counterparty, and a clone cannot inherit it. The atlas ledger charges a 48-hour settlement delay per new receipt, so cloning costs a full handoff cycle plus a forfeited plume deposit if the co-signer rejects the transfer. Honest agents reuse existing receipts at zero cost; an attacker pays one deposit and delay per clone.
